reasons: The excerpt explicitly equates the good landing-page structure with a VSSL-script structure and describes the sequence of hook, problem, unique mechanism, objections, proof, risk reversal, and CTA.
The cold-VSSL context and the instruction that the hook reinforce VSSL language are directly stated.
The source explicitly says to be mobile first, states that 60% to 95% of traffic may come from mobile depending on the brand, and says 10% of effort goes to desktop.
The source supports progressive split testing for an 8- to 9-figure brand with sufficient traffic and volume.

The prerequisite that 'The program is set up correctly' is circular relative to the action to set up the program. The source presents correct setup as an implementation requirement, not as a condition that must already be met before setup begins.

The source instructs the reader to list possible changes, score impact, confidence, and ease out of 10, multiply the scores, sort the results, implement the highest score first, and work down over time.
The candidate appropriately notes transcription inconsistency around the ICE terminology without adding a different scoring method.

The warning accurately retains the source's condition that a four-week skin-firmness claim should not be made if the product cannot deliver that result, along with the stated returns and repeat-purchase consequences.
The source supports evaluating actual efficacy by messaging angle, particularly while spinning up new angles and concepts.

The candidate's title and claim identify returns, whether the product fulfills the need, and 365-day LTV, but its action only says to be on top of efficacy. Revise the action to include monitoring returns and 365 LTV by angle so that it represents the full supplied advice rather than fragmenting it.
The source explicitly advises looking at revenue per visitor or contribution per visitor rather than conversion rate and gives the stated reasons conversion rate can be misleading.

The candidate directly reflects the recap instruction to use specific, claim-matched proof, real reviews, and photos first, while not prioritizing trust badges or other items that do not move the needle.
The source explicitly instructs removing checkout friction and avoiding the earlier-mentioned causes of cart abandonment to maximize completed purchases.
The candidate correctly marks the actual abandonment reasons as unavailable in this excerpt rather than inventing them.
The action and click-to-landing-page trigger are supported by the source.

The asserted depends_on relationship to the VSSL-style landing-page-structure candidate is not stated. The source connects the landing page to the ad narrative but does not establish completion of that other candidate as a prerequisite for this action.
The action accurately reflects the source's above-the-fold clarity, product-definition, and hierarchy guidance, while correctly noting that the five questions are absent from the excerpt.

The asserted depends_on relationship to the VSSL-style landing-page-structure candidate is unsupported. The source calls clarity and hierarchy an important recommendation in its own right and does not make it contingent on that other action.
The source recommends watching the 40-minute YouTube video and opening it in a new tab for viewers unfamiliar with VSSLs, and describes the video's stated scope.

omissions.description: For the specific low-ticket offer being discussed, determine how to bundle it rather than leaving it as-is.
omissions.quote: I think this offer is too low ticket, and we need to figure out how to bundle this up.

source_limitations: The excerpt begins mid-sentence and refers to earlier material that is not supplied, including the core five questions and the specific reasons customers abandon carts.

The excerpt contains transcript ambiguities and apparent errors, including "impact, confident, and confidence," "eye score," and "8 N figures," so some terminology cannot be resolved from this source alone.
The source gives no operational definition of a correctly configured CRO program, progressive split tests, revenue per visitor, contribution per visitor, or a one-of-one angle.
Numerical ranges, eligibility thresholds, and performance or LTV consequences are presenter assertions in this excerpt; no underlying data, test design, or evidence is supplied to evaluate them.
